references.text: Joseph's bones are carried out of Egypt, as he had requested.
By faith Joseph spoke about the coming exodus of Israel's children from Egypt and gave instructions concerning his bones.
Joseph's bones, which the children of Israel brought up from Egypt, were buried in Shechem – the final fulfillment of his wish.
Joseph tells his brothers that God will surely visit them and bring them out of Egypt – the background for the oath in verse 25.
Theological parallel: Both prophesy God's faithfulness in bringing the people back to the land.
Theological contrast and fulfillment: Joshua's entry into the land completes Joseph's exodus from Egypt.
Prophetic precursor and fulfillment: God's promise to bring the people out (46:4) is repeated as a command in Joseph's testament (50:25).
